title: Content-Security-Policy without object-src or default-src
description: The policy neither sets object-src nor supplies a default-src fallback, so object, embed and applet loading is unconstrained. object-src is a fetch directive: when it is absent the browser applies default-src, which is why a policy that sets default-src is not reported here.
remediation: Add object-src 'none' (or rely on a restrictive default-src) so plugins and embedded objects cannot load from arbitrary origins.
limitation: Fallback-aware directive check: a policy that sets default-src constrains object loading through the fallback and is not reported. A policy that sets object-src explicitly is out of scope for this check, and a policy delivered by a meta element cannot be seen. Because the check requires both object-src and default-src to be absent, every case it reports is also reported by DPK-DAST-087 (missing default-src); this rule adds the object-loading explanation, not a second condition.
